'''Myōken-ji''' (妙見寺) is a {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|qid=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism|1=Tiantai}} temple located in {{ill|Takasaki|en|Takasaki|qid=Q336438|lt=Takasaki|1=Takasaki}}, Gunma Prefecture, Japan. Its mountain name (''sangō'') is Sankosan, and its cloister name (''ingō'') is Kisshōin. The temple's principal image is {{ill|Shakyamuni Tathāgata Buddha|ja|釈迦如来|1=Shakyamuni Tathāgata|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shakyamuni Tathāgata Buddha|qq=}}.

== History ==
The founding date of this temple is unclear, but it is traditionally said to have been established in either [[:en:Wadō|Wadō]] 7 (714) or {{ill|Reiki|en|Reiki|qid=Q183057|lt=Reiki|1=Reiki}} 1 (715) by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadaaki|ja|藤原忠明|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tadaaki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a local official in {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|qid=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province|1=Kōzuke Province}}.

According to the "Hanazono Star God Record" (花園星神記), Tadaaki once stayed at the temple. Awakening at midnight, he noticed a bright light rising in the northwest direction. Curious, he sent retainers to investigate and discovered the light emanated from the Kobushi Pond in Reimizu Town. They retrieved a rare turtle with red eyes and a white neck from the water. When Tadaaki presented this turtle to the emperor, it was so highly esteemed that the era name was changed to Reiki ("Holy Turtle").

The temple is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en|Shoku Nihongi|qid=Q611399|lt=Shoku Nihongi|1=Shoku Nihongi}}, compiled in {{ill|Enryaku|en|Enryaku|qid=Q1373176|lt=Enryaku|1=Enryaku}} 16 (797), confirming its long-standing history. Previously known as "Shichiseizan Sokusaiji," it has been a site of devotion to {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken Bosatsu|1=Myōken}} and was also called "Hitsuji Myōken" (Sheep Myōken). Some scholars link the temple to the {{ill|Tago Stele|en|Tago Stele|qid=Q11431029|lt=Tako Kō Monument|1=Tago Stele}}, particularly its reference to "sheep."

During the {{ill|Tengyō no Ran|en|Tengyō no Ran|qid=Q2975322|lt=Jōhei-Tengyō War|1=Tengyō no Ran}}, {{ill|Taira no Yoshifumi|en|Taira no Yoshifumi|qid=Q11483528|lt=Taira no Yoshifumi|1=Taira no Yoshifumi}}, cornered in the Battle of Someyagawa, followed a mysterious voice to the temple. There, a monk entrusted him with the "Seven-Star Sword," enabling him to gain the protection of Myōken Bosatsu. Myōken deities revered at {{ill|Chichibu Shrine|en|Chichibu Shrine|qid=Q2963366|lt=Chichibu Shrine|1=Chichibu Shrine}} and {{ill|Chiba Shrine|en|Chiba Shrine|qid=Q11406700|lt=Chiba Shrine|1=Chiba Shrine}} were enshrined from this temple.

In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the temple received a red-seal letter from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, granting it official recognition and support.

== Access ==
